coaching.headline: Lt. Belica's rotation answered an early two-kill hole, then kills went fourteen to six with both Fangtooths and the Genesis Core. A proper fucking beating.
coaching.team: Sevarog killed Greystone twice before the team scored, and Lt. Belica answered the second from mid 22 seconds later for the team's first kill. The kill count was level at two and again at four apiece. From there the team took ten of the last twelve kills. The team also took both Fangtooths, the Genesis Core, fourteen river buffs to six and two enemy outer towers while losing one. The only Fangtooth or Prime objective the enemy got was the Mini Prime, taken with nobody on the team dead.

focus.title: Turn won fights into objectives
focus.action: After a won fight, one player calls the nearest live objective or enemy structure and the team walks there together. When the Mini Prime is up and enemies are on death timers, the Prime is the call, ahead of chasing another kill.

19.call: Two plays on opposite sides of the map. Sevarog killed Greystone on the offlane and the allied offlane outer tower fell soon after. On the duo lane, Murdock killed Serath and Lt. Belica rotated in from mid to kill Neon, and the team then took the enemy duo lane outer tower and the second Fangtooth.

13.7.call: Two separate picks on opposite sides of the map, not one fight: GRIM.exe killed Murdock on the duo lane and Mourn killed Greystone on the offlane. That drew the enemy level at four apiece, and the team took the first Fangtooth shortly after.

15.8.call: Lt. Belica killed Mourn and Wukong killed Neon, with no allied deaths. The fight went 2-0, and the enemy took the Mini Prime in the same stretch with nobody on the team dead.

22.2.call: Two plays on opposite sides of the map. Greystone killed Sevarog on the offlane, while on the duo lane Murdock killed Serath and GRIM.exe and Neon killed Steel. The team then took an enemy outer tower and the Genesis Core.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Murdock was broke for a carry: two completed items, the fourth-most gold on the team and farm under the Murdock norm. Between fights, Murdock takes the nearest safe wave so Vanquisher and Imperator land before the next big fight.
Mr_Meat31 still turned GRIM.exe into a piñata: three kills on GRIM.exe, one death all game, the most kills in the game and the most hero damage on the team.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Zero deaths, the most objective damage in the game and both Fangtooths to the team. Goldilocks324 ran a clean fucking jungle on Wukong, and Serath finished without a single kill.

Four enemy wards cleared, every clear the team got, against one ward placed. Wukong sweeps the approach before every Fangtooth and Prime contest, and calls for a laner's ward on the cleared pit entrance.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Sevarog killed Greystone three times, first blood included. A shit exchange rate and the most deaths on the team. When Subjugate lands, Greystone stays inside the zone until the chain breaks; leaving it means a stun.
Still, Cuban Noobster ate the most damage and did the most healing in the game on Greystone, then took down Sevarog in the final fight. Real meat-wall numbers.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Willy Guggenheim left an unopened mid twice for kills on the offlane and duo lane, died zero times, finished the richest player in the game, and mid never lost a structure. Filthy, greedy, correct.

Hero damage per minute still sat under the recorded Lt. Belica norm with all that gold. Neon stacked mana with Azure Core and Combustion, so Lt. Belica parks Void Drone on Neon before firing Neural Disruptor.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Proper support shift from Xeebs on Steel: tied for the most assists in the game, a hand in over a third of the team's kills, wards above the recorded Steel norm and the second-most damage mitigated on the team.
Mourn placed the most wards in the game and Steel cleared none. When the duo wave is shoved, Steel spends that window sweeping the duo-side river for Mourn's wards, with a sentry if one is equipped.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.matchup: Murdock and Steel faced carry GRIM.exe and support Mourn. GRIM.exe's basic attacks deal magical damage, Energy Shield blocks the next enemy ability and GTFO homes in on one hero; Instant Reload lets GTFO execute heroes at very low health and be recast. Mourn pulls with Abduct, mesmerizes with Beguile and shreds both armors with Contagion. Murdock killed GRIM.exe three times and GRIM.exe killed Murdock once, and the enemy duo died once before the ten-minute mark while the allied duo never did. When Energy Shield goes up, Buckshot goes first so Long Arm of the Law is not the ability blocked.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Lightning Hawk builds Momentum while moving or landing basic attacks and empowers a slowing hit at full stacks. Tainted Rounds cuts healing on basic attacks and adds on-hit damage that grows as the target's health drops; Serath had the second-most healing in the game and Mourn's Contagion heals allies. Both items add critical chance and attack speed, which feeds the charged Shots Fired attack. Neither adds armor or health against an enemy team dealing mostly magical damage, and Sevarog dealt the most hero damage in the game.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.eternal: Vermis adds maximum-health physical damage on every third consecutive basic attack on the same hero within a short window, and Serration adds missing-health damage to that hit, which suits finishing GRIM.exe and Serath. Melting Point only pays against targets above a high physical armor threshold, and Sevarog and Mourn were the only enemies carrying physical armor items. Breach is the second-minor alternative: Long Arm of the Law already ignores physical armor, and the shred after an ultimate hit helps follow-up physical damage from Murdock, Wukong and Greystone, trading the threshold bonus.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.augment: Justice's Reach makes the charged Shots Fired attack pierce units and adds range, so the empowered shot can reach past minions or a frontliner. Sting Operation is the alternative, adding two Static Trap charges and larger traps, trading the longer charged shot for more roots against divers. Martial Law adds Long Arm of the Law damage and gold on hero kills. Charged-shot hits are not recorded.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.crest: Pacifier's Adrenalize dashes a short distance and empowers the next physical damage instance, hitting much harder on targets at low health, and a hero kill soon after allows a recast. Murdock's basic attacks, Buckshot and Long Arm of the Law all deal physical damage, so the empowered hit has plenty to ride on. The crest's lifesteal pairs with steady basic attacks. Activations and resets are not recorded.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.improvement: The winning core is Lightning Hawk, Vanquisher and Imperator; Murdock finished Lightning Hawk and Tainted Rounds only. Vanquisher adds physical penetration and executes heroes at very low health, and Imperator raises critical strike damage. Greystone's Tainted Blade and Steel's Tainted Guard already covered anti-heal, so Tainted Rounds is the slot to compare against the core's damage. With five kills and one death, no build impact is proven either way.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.matchup: Wukong's jungle opponent was Serath, who marks a target with Heaven's Fury, vanishes for a string of strikes and then teleports to it, slows with Chastise, dives with Ascend and powers up with Heresy; Crushing Descent adds a short stun to Ascend. Serath built Sky Splitter and Spectra, sustained basic-attack damage with lifesteal. Wukong and Murdock killed Serath twice each and Lt. Belica once, and Serath finished without a kill while posting the second-most healing in the game. Wukong's other kill was Neon. Across the match Sevarog dealt the most hero damage in the game.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.build: Manta Scythe adds attack speed, lifesteal and extra damage on minions and small monsters, plus bonus damage on targets with no nearby ally. Infernum ignites a target after four stacks of Kindling for maximum-health damage, more against enemies with bonus armor, and Sevarog and Mourn both carried physical armor items. The Perforator ignores part of physical armor and slows on ability damage. None of the three adds armor or health, and the matchup flag notes no magical armor against four magical damage dealers.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.eternal: Lotus randomly grants small damage, haste, movement speed or health bonuses on a timer and on takedowns. Early Bloom grants an extra level on reaching a set level, and Immaculate cuts damage taken while near full health, so that protection fades once a fight starts biting. Masterpiece is the first-minor alternative, adding stacking damage and movement speed on kills, trading the free level for a bonus that grows with Wukong's kills.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.augment: Masterful Mimicry adds one more maximum clone and generates a Hair stack on a timer, so the ultimate spawns clones without needing every stack from hitting enemies. From Up High is the alternative, uncapping High Impact's height bonus, trading clone pressure for a bigger Body-stance slam. Prosperous Path adds gold or missing-health restoration on kills depending on stance. Clone uptime is not recorded.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.crest: Nex's Reap dashes a short distance, damages nearby heroes and slows, and hits harder with the Sow charge stored from recent hero damage, a smaller share from area abilities. That rewards landing basic attacks and abilities on a hero before pressing Reap. The crest also adds physical penetration, stacking with Manta Scythe and The Perforator. Activations are not recorded.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.improvement: The winning core is Manta Scythe, Infernum and Syonic Echo; Wukong built The Perforator instead of Syonic Echo. Syonic Echo adds lifesteal, and each ability cast gives the next three basic attacks bonus attack speed with a basic attack reset on melee heroes, at the cost of The Perforator's armor penetration and slow. Dread is the magical armor comparison, blocking part of magical damage from heroes. With zero deaths and the most objective damage in the game, the build is a sound keep.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.matchup: Greystone's offlane opponent was Sevarog, who fears with Phantom Rush, steals maximum health with Siphon, chains enemies with Subjugate and stuns any who leave the zone, and knocks heroes back with Colossal Blow; Unholy Pursuit resets Phantom Rush when Colossal Blow hits a hero. Sevarog built Fire Blossom, Elafrost and Fist Of Razuul: health, physical armor and self-healing, with every ability dealing magical damage. Sevarog killed Greystone three times, first blood included, and Greystone killed Sevarog once. Sevarog dealt the most hero damage in the game.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.build: Overlord cleaves damage around the target on basic attacks and grows health from kills. Tainted Blade cuts healing on physical damage, which is all of Greystone's damage, aimed at Sevarog's Fist Of Razuul heal and Serath's lifesteal; ability damage on a blighted target adds a damage-taken debuff. Neither item adds armor, against an enemy team dealing mostly magical damage. Stoicism's armor that grows with missing health is physical armor only, no help against Sevarog's magical abilities.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.eternal: Krix adds maximum health and size. Voracity restores a little health and gold on unit kills, and Cannibalism permanently adds health on takedowns, with one kill and no assists to feed the stacks. Regenerative Tissue is the first-minor alternative, regenerating health after a stretch without hero damage, trading unit-kill sustain for recovery between trades with Sevarog. Feeding Frenzy is the second-minor alternative, adding attack speed per nearby enemy hero for faster Overlord cleaves.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.augment: Tainted Oath makes Sacred Oath apply Blight, overlapping with Tainted Blade, which already blights on physical hits. Close Cut is the alternative, making Make Way hit the nearest enemy unit harder, which suits close trades with Sevarog, and Make Way already shreds physical armor against Fire Blossom and Elafrost. Imperial Soul makes Stone Forged Soul hit harder in a larger area. Blight uptime is not recorded.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.crest: Saphir's Mantle's Atlas briefly increases Greystone's size and maximum health, damages nearby heroes and permanently adds maximum health from that damage. The crest also adds a little of both armors, the only magical armor Greystone carried against Sevarog's magical abilities. Activations are not recorded.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.improvement: The winning core is Overlord, Rapture and Aegis Of Agawar; Greystone finished Overlord and Tainted Blade, with neither Rapture nor Aegis Of Agawar. Aegis Of Agawar raises total armors by a percentage, but with no magical armor item the percentage only scales base magical armor and Saphir's Mantle's small amount. Mistmeadow Buckler is the sharper comparison against Sevarog: physical power, flat magical armor and a charge-based magical damage block, at the cost of Tainted Blade's anti-heal, a swap that only holds while Murdock keeps Tainted Rounds and Steel keeps Tainted Guard.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.matchup: Lt. Belica's mid opponent was Neon, who dashes with Erase Vector, sends L.I.N.X out and back, slows with Data Burst, which also mesmerizes when Overclocked, and Overclocks every basic ability during Final Thread. Neon built Azure Core, Combustion and Overseer, so Final Thread hits harder and heals Neon on hero damage. Lt. Belica killed Neon once and Neon never killed Lt. Belica. Across the match Lt. Belica also killed Sevarog, Mourn and Serath, and Sevarog dealt the most hero damage in the game.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.build: Combustion adds bonus damage around the target on ability damage, recharging faster on hero damage. Noxia marks a hero on ability damage and pays maximum-health damage when a separate ability follows, so Seismic Assault into Void Bomb or Neural Disruptor is the natural sequence. Wraith Leggings adds magical penetration and bonus ability damage on heroes below a health threshold. No enemy completed a magical armor item, so the penetration only had base magical armor to cut. Lt. Belica completed the full winning core.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.eternal: Aion grants mana regeneration on spell casts and gold from spell damage to heroes, a fit for a mid laner who finished with the most gold in the game. Bottomless Vial restores a potion charge and adds permanent magical power for each river buff Lt. Belica kills, and the team took fourteen river buffs to six, though river buff credit is not recorded per player. Runic Focus adds magical power from current mana, fed by Combustion's mana. Sacrifice is the first-minor alternative, refilling missing mana on ability hits and hero kills, trading the river-buff power.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.augment: Combat Veteran pays a trickle of experience every second, scaling with level, plus a little movement speed. Experience speeds up maxing abilities, and Innovation upgrades each maxed ability and adds ability haste; a maxed Seismic Assault stuns longer. Pulsefire Rounds is the damage alternative, adding on-hit damage to SMG fire between casts, aimed at the hero damage per minute that sat under the recorded Lt. Belica norm. Level timing is not recorded.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.crest: Soulbearer's Anima wraps Lt. Belica in a shield and adds magical lifesteal and movement speed for several seconds, turning a spell rotation into sustain. With zero deaths, the crest is a sound keep; Epoch's stasis is the draft alternative only if Sevarog or Serath start reaching Lt. Belica. Activations are not recorded.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.improvement: Lt. Belica completed Combustion, Noxia and Wraith Leggings with the most gold in the game. With no enemy magical armor item to cut, the next slot leans toward raw damage: Oblivion Crown raises magical power by a percentage, aimed at the hero damage per minute under norm. A defensive slot only earns a place if Sevarog's Phantom Rush and Subjugate start catching Lt. Belica. Zero deaths makes the current path a sound keep.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.matchup: Steel and Murdock faced support Mourn and carry GRIM.exe. Mourn pulls with Abduct, mesmerizes with Beguile, heals allies and shreds both armors with Contagion, and darkens enemy vision with Eclipse; Nightstalker adds movement speed during Eclipse. Mourn built Dynamo and Golem's Gift and placed the most wards in the game. GRIM.exe's basic attacks deal magical damage and GTFO homes in on one hero. Steel killed GRIM.exe once, and Neon got Steel's only death in the final fight.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Xenia shields an ally standing close on a per-target cooldown and adds both armors, the only completed allied item with magical armor against four magical damage dealers. Dynamo makes an immobilized enemy take more damage for a short time, which Shield Bash and Shield Slam stuns trigger. Tainted Guard cuts the healing of any hero basic-attacking Steel and bleeds that hero, with Serath's lifesteal and Sevarog's Fist Of Razuul heal as targets.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: Krix adds maximum health and size. Regenerative Tissue regenerates health after a stretch without hero damage, and Cannibalism permanently adds health on takedowns, fed by Steel's five takedowns. Festering Wounds is the first-minor alternative, making immobilizing effects cut enemy healing, but Tainted Guard, Tainted Rounds and Tainted Blade already covered anti-heal, so Regenerative Tissue is the sound keep.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.augment: Heavy Metal turns Steel's total physical and magical armor into magical on-hit damage on heavy punches and Shield Bash, and Xenia, Dynamo and Tainted Guard each add armor, so the bonus grows with every item here. Adaptive Force is the alternative, giving Force Shield two charges and a shorter cooldown at a smaller size, more walls against ranged projectiles. Bulldozer adds damage reduction to Bull Rush. Bonus damage dealt is not recorded.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.crest: Sanctification's Safeguard shields Steel and nearby heroes, with tenacity while the shield holds against Beguile's mesmerize and Phantom Rush's fear. The crest also pays passive gold each second, raises the ward cap and gives diminishing minion gold. Activations are not recorded.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.improvement: The winning core is Xenia, Dynamo and Gaia Greaves; Steel built Tainted Guard instead of Gaia Greaves. Gaia Greaves adds health, physical armor, movement stacks spent on a bonus-damage basic attack and higher jumps, at the cost of Tainted Guard's anti-heal and bleed on basic attackers. Neither adds magical armor, and Cybernetic Shell turns only a small share of bonus physical armor into magical armor. With one death and the second-most damage mitigated on the team, the build is a sound keep.

threats: Chain-CC risk (1 hard-CC abilities, ~0.5s of lockdown): Mourn Abduct (pull). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Heal-stacking: Mourn. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought 3 items of it.
Enemy is 4/5 magical — one magic-resist item goes a long way.
Dive threat on our backline: Serath. Assign peel for the carry and ward the flanks.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Lt. Belica Neural Disruptor (silence 0.5s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Static Trap root → Buckshot → Hot Pursuit AS → Long Arm of the Law global snipe
ourKits.winCondition: trap for the root, then out-range with Shots Fired and finish with the global ult
ourKits.passive: every 5th basic is a long-range bonus shot
ourKits.playWith: frontline/peel to protect his low mobility
ourKits.playAgainst: almost no escape — engage past the trap and he dies

ourKits.combo: Windsurge engage → Cyclebreaker damage-reduction spin → clones from 84000 Hairs
ourKits.winCondition: stance-dance for damage or tankiness and overwhelm with clones
ourKits.playWith: a team that fights alongside his clones
ourKits.playAgainst: AoE clears his clones; CC him during the damage-reduction window

ourKits.combo: Assault The Gates leap → Make Way armor shred → Sacred Oath empowered basic → Stone Forged Soul stasis ult
ourKits.winCondition: front-line aggressively and reset the fight with the stasis heal
ourKits.playWith: a team that fights while he soaks and stasis-resets
ourKits.playAgainst: don't waste burst into his stasis — wait it out; anti-heal cuts the ult heal

ourKits.combo: Seismic Assault knockup → Void Bomb → Neural Disruptor silence ult, Void Drone mana drain
ourKits.winCondition: knock up + silence a target and burst with missing-HP scaling
ourKits.playAgainst: dodge Seismic Assault; she's immobile — dive when ult is down

ourKits.combo: Bull Rush knockback → Force Shield wall → Shield Slam knockup+stun ult, Shield Bash %hp
ourKits.winCondition: peel the carry with walls/knockups or engage with Shield Slam
ourKits.playWith: a carry he can wall for and peel
ourKits.playAgainst: his Force Shield blocks projectiles — reposition around it; bait Shield Slam

enemyKits.combo: Energy Shield block → Displacement Blast → Assault Mode → GTFO lockon ult
enemyKits.winCondition: out-trade with Pulsefire and the spell-shield, finish with GTFO
enemyKits.playWith: peel so he can free-cast in Assault Mode
enemyKits.playAgainst: bait Energy Shield, then commit; dodge GTFO's slow channel

enemyKits.combo: Ascend dive → Heaven's Fury multi-strike → Chastise slow → Heresy form ult, resets on takedowns
enemyKits.winCondition: dive the backline and snowball Heresy resets
enemyKits.playWith: a frontline that creates her dive angle
enemyKits.playAgainst: peel the backline — deny the first kill and her resets dry up

enemyKits.combo: Abduct pull → Contagion ally-heal bugs → Beguile damage-reduction → Eclipse vision-denial ult
enemyKits.winCondition: pull a target in and sustain the team through the brawl
enemyKits.playWith: burst that punishes his pulled target
enemyKits.playAgainst: respect the long Abduct channel/range; anti-heal blunts Contagion

enemyKits.combo: Phantom Rush → Subjugate root → Siphon → Colossal Blow
enemyKits.winCondition: stack Souls to snowball Siphon and lock down with the root
enemyKits.passive: ability kills grant permanent Soul stacks (HP + damage)
enemyKits.playWith: a team that converts his root into kills
enemyKits.playAgainst: deny his last-hits early to starve Souls; dodge the slow Subjugate
